root_cause: rich.pretty.traverse() walks a dataclass by iterating fields(obj) where field.repr is true and calling getattr(obj, field.name). A field declared with field(init=False) and no default is never set on the instance, so getattr raises AttributeError and console.print/pretty_repr crash (e.g. in pretty tracebacks).
best_solution: In the dataclass branch of traverse() in rich/pretty.py, filter the field generator to `field.repr and hasattr(obj, field.name)`, so fields that exist in the class definition but were never assigned on the instance are skipped. A dataclass whose only field is unset then renders through the Node's existing empty form, `BadDataclass()`. Reasoning from the statement: 'missing field in dataclass' means a declared field that is absent from the instance. The only code that reads dataclass fields generically is the fields()+getattr loop, so it has to tolerate the missing attribute.
acceptable_alternatives: Wrap getattr in try/except AttributeError and skip the field, or use getattr with a sentinel default and skip the sentinel. Either output must be exactly 'BadDataclass()'. Showing a placeholder or error value for the field would fail the exact-string assertion.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_pretty.py::test_dataclass_no_attribute: @dataclass(eq=False) class BadDataclass: item: int = field(init=False); console.print(BadDataclass()) captured output must equal exactly 'BadDataclass()\n' (no exception, and the unset field is omitted entirely).
locating_signals: The statement is only the PR title 'fix for missing field in dataclass' plus a link to issue #3417. The words 'dataclass' and 'field' point to rich/pretty.py's dataclass branch (fields(obj) / getattr loop), but no function is named. The key detail, that the missing field comes from field(init=False), is only in the linked issue, which the agent cannot see. The issue itself cites pretty.py#L782, the exact failing line.
our_outcome_summary: All four configs failed (v4/v6/v7/v8 kaggle_env_pass=false); every hidden-test run raised AttributeError: 'BadDataclass' object has no attribute 'item' at rich/pretty.py:786. v4 (295s, 102 calls) spent its budget writing about 15 scratch repro scripts for field(repr=False) cases and never touched rich/pretty.py. v6 read 'missing field' as repr=False fields and added empty=f'{cls}()' to the attrs Node (the wrong branch, and the dataclass Node already had empty=); it left the getattr loop alone. v7 added an unused is_dataclass flag to Node. v8 produced an empty patch. None of them tried the init=False (unset attribute) case, so they never reproduced the real crash.
generalizable_lesson: When the statement is a terse title plus an issue link the agent can't open, list the concrete ways the phrase could break before editing ('missing field' could be an unset attribute via init=False, repr=False, or a deleted attr). Write a tiny repro for each and pick the one that actually raises. A real bug crashes or gives wrong output, so a repro that runs fine means you guessed the wrong bug. For any generic introspection loop (fields()/vars()/__slots__ + getattr), guard against attributes that are declared but never set, using hasattr or try/except, and keep the output exactly the same as the no-field case.
